speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for Transport what has been the total amount of expenditure incurred to date by Singapore on the High Speed Rail project and what are the terms specified in the bilateral agreement in relation to compensation claims upon termination of the agreement by either party.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Subsequent to that, at the request of Malaysia, the HSR Project was further suspended until 31 December 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Malaysia has now decided not to proceed with the HSR Project.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will include various abortive costs but not land acquisition costs since the value of the land can be recovered.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The compensation amount for the termination and schedule for payment are specified in our agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In addition, there is a small component of miscellaneous abortive costs for the suspension of the Project requested by Malaysia that Singapore is currently verifying, before we send to Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Due to Singapore’s confidentiality obligations under the HSR Bilateral Agreement, we are unable to reveal the exact terms in relation to the compensation for the termination of the HSR Project.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We look forward to continue to build good relations and work closely with Malaysia to improve connectivity in other ways, and in many other fields, for the mutual benefit of the people of both countries.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is, now that we know that the high speed rail has officially been cancelled, if the Minister can share with the Members of the House what were some of the substantive points of differences that cannot be breached that led to the cancellation?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And in relation to compensation, I note earlier in July 2018 that former Transport Minister Mr Khaw Boon Wan said that the total cost incurred back then was exceeding $250 million which is expected to exceed $300 million by the end of 2018.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, in relation to the expenditure already incurred, if Minister could share the details on what is the difference and whether or not we will be able to recover the full amount of the expenditure, excluding land acquisition costs, as the Minister had mentioned, and if so, when should we expect some form of conclusion on this?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Then-Minister Khaw Boon Wan did mention the figure of S$250 million.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: He also mentioned that costs continue to be incurred and, therefore, it may reach S$300 million or so later.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Will we be able to claim the full amount?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The amount to be compensated, as I have mentioned, and the schedule for payment, these are specified in the agreements.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is a fixed amount specified in the agreements.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we have started the process of compensation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the first question, it is an important one – the substantive point of difference.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Singapore and Malaysia signed the HSR Bilateral Agreement – we call it HSR BA – in 2016.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And that is after three years of negotiations to implement the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Subsequently, both Parties signed two supplementary agreements relating to the suspension of the construction of the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the first supplementary agreement was signed in 2018, to suspend the construction of the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: By then, it would have been extended by two and a half years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I will refer to the HSR BA, subsequently amended by the supplementary agreements, generically as the "HSR Agreements" as a short form.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the HSR Agreements are legally binding international agreements.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Parties come to the table as equals, discuss the various terms, such as how to structure and implement the cross-border HSR Project, and the rights and obligations placed on both Parties.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As Members know, this process involves understanding each other's concerns, addressing them, striking compromises and finding mutually acceptable common ground.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Singapore was fully committed to carry out our obligations under the HSR BA.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But Malaysia felt that circumstances had changed, including due to COVID-19, and proposed several changes to the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Be clear about this, which is, Singapore was not obligated to agree to any of such changes because we had signed an agreement in 2016 already.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But, notwithstanding, we considered them in good faith.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As the HSR is a cross-border service, it must be a single train system operating between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because neither country has the expertise and experience in operating an HSR, we agreed, under the HSR BA, to appoint a best-in-class industry player through an open and transparent international tender to assume the role of the AssetsCo.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Once appointed, the AssetsCo would supply the train system, operate the network, ensure that appropriate priority is given to cross-border HSR service vis-a-vis Malaysia's domestic service, and AssetsCo would be accountable to both countries, that is, Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To Singapore, AssetsCo is the centrepiece of the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is necessary to ensure that the interests of both countries are protected.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This will minimise the possibility of future disagreements and disputes over the long duration of the Project, lasting decades.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Singapore, therefore, informed Malaysia that the removal of the AssetsCo constituted a fundamental departure from the HSR BA and could not be accepted.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Malaysia has since decided to allow the HSR BA to be terminated.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In these circumstances, it has to compensate Singapore, in accordance with the HSR Agreements.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Now that the HSR BA has been terminated, Singapore is willing to discuss any new proposal on a KL-Singapore HSR from Malaysia in good faith, but starting from a clean slate.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First of all, I would like to thank the MOT team for putting in a lot of good work done that led to an agreement after four years of negotiations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But, alas, Malaysia proposed changes to the agreement and it did not go through.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But following up on the Minister's answer just now, also for the sake of transparency, can the Minister share why another extension of the bilateral agreement would not have been possible and whether a further extension would have allowed some room for further discussions to be made to reach an agreement?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Another question is whether Singapore is open to HSR-like projects in the future.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And then, there was a second request from Malaysia to extend it until 31 December 2020, that is, another six months, which we were not obligated to agree, but we agreed to it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think there will have to be a finality to the suspension and extension of the Project.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Having said that, there is a fundamental difference which I have explained earlier with regard to the removal of the AssetsCo.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Whether we are open to future discussions, of course, we are.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it should be on a clean slate, after we have settled the current HSR BA.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: First, is there any impact of the cancellation of HSR on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS)?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Second, what would be the impact of the HSR cancellation on the development of the Jurong Regional Centre?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Although I have moved from Jurong GRC to West Coast GRC, but many of the West Coast GRC divisions are very close to the Jurong Regional Centre.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I hope the Minister can give a good reply.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The short answer to the first question is no.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for Jurong Regional Centre, let me assure the House that MND had started planning to transform Jurong as early as 2008.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the Jurong Lake District is part of a broader effort to develop urban centres outside of our CBD and our city centre.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The plans for Jurong Lake District, or JLD were, therefore, developed well before Malaysia proposed the current HSR Project in 2012.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It was only much later, in 2015, that we decided to locate the Singapore terminus of the HSR in Jurong.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The termination of the HSR Project, therefore, does not affect the overall impetus and vision for JLD, although some details may need to be adjusted along the way.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When completed, this will be the largest commercial and regional centre outside of our city centre, bringing many jobs, business and recreation opportunities for Singaporeans and Singapore companies.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The land parcels that the Government has acquired are still needed to realise these plans.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For example, the Jurong Country Club site will provide for new mixed-use developments and community facilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Raffles Country Club site is also still needed for the Cross Island Line's western depot and the Integrated Train Testing Centre.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will be able to realise the full potential of the land to benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Prior to COVID-19, the Singapore-Kuala Lumpur air route was one of the busiest in the world, with more than four million passengers flying this route every year.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The HSR Project was meant to shorten the travel time between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur from about five hours by air to just 90 minutes, and provide greater access to both cities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My first question is, what is the impact of the HSR's cancellation on the attractiveness of Singapore as the region's premier air hub and on the SIA Group as a whole?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My second question is, how many staff at SG HSR Pte Ltd have been impacted by the project's cancellation and how many have already been redeployed to other job roles?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And what are the manpower plans for the remaining staff that have yet to be redeployed?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the Member just now meant five hours by car, not five hours by air.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What is the impact of HSR termination by Malaysia on our aviation air hub?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I have mentioned earlier, there are some reasons given as to why the Project was terminated and the impact on air hub was cited in some media reports.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as mentioned, our main concern was the removal of the AssetsCo.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Express Rail Link is an existing train system, not an HSR, and runs at half the full speed of HSR.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, should we have proceeded, there would have been many technical issues to resolve.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But having said that, the main concern for us was the removal of the AssetsCo.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it is precisely because of this heavy air traffic between Singapore and KL that we believe that the HSR Project was viable, mutually beneficial and strategic for the long term.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, Singapore will always assess the cost benefit of such major infrastructure projects from a national and long-term perspective, and not just from the perspective of one company or one industry.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the Member's second question about manpower, 80 staff are affected.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Out of the 80, 70 or so have been redeployed to LTA and the other 10, we are looking them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are confident we can redeploy all of them in LTA or within the larger transport eco-system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are many important projects that are happening, and there will always be a need for good people, such as those 80 people working on the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: What is the reasoning behind the Malaysian government's reason for the change on their position on the AssetsCo?
